title: Polyglot SDK Sprintbox — Minimal starter patterns: CLI, Next.js, FastAPI, Go server with streaming + retry conventions
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create a compact, opinionated starter kit that demonstrates idiomatic usage patterns for Redwood SDKs in Python, TypeScript, and Go. Deliverables: 1) minimal Next.js app (TS) with streaming chat and function/tool call example; 2) FastAPI example (Python) showing resumable streaming, prefix caching hooks, and retry/backoff policy integration; 3) Go HTTP server example that demonstrates single-request streaming and KV cache reuse; 4) small CLI (TS/Python) examples showing resumable tokens, graceful cancellation, and deterministic retry semantics; 5) cookbook snippets explaining recommended retry parameters, batching/throughput knobs, and common pitfalls. Focus: ergonomics for streaming+retries, clear README patterns, reproducible dev flow (local + remote API key), and tests/examples that can be copy-pasted by customers.
acceptance_criteria: Each language has a runnable example that starts with one command and documents env vars
Streaming examples include both client-side handling and server-side helper abstractions (resume, cancel, partial output) documented
Retry policy is explicit in examples (idempotency keys where appropriate) and a short cookbook section explains when to use each policy
Examples include small integration tests (smoke) and a script that can run against hosted Redwood or a local mock server
README includes cost/latency guidance and recommended SDK config for low-latency interactive workloads
PRs merged with at least one engineering and one DX (developer experience) review signoff
tasks: Design starterkit structure and minimal API surface for sample apps
Implement Next.js TS example: streaming chat, function calling, live UI partials
Implement FastAPI Python example: streaming generator, prefix cache hook, retry decorator
Implement Go HTTP server example: single connection streaming with KV cache reuse
Author CLI examples: ts-node quick-cli and python script with graceful shutdown
Write cookbook.md with retry/backoff presets, batch sizing heuristics, and streaming pitfalls
Add smoke tests and CI job to validate examples against mock server
Collect DX feedback and iterate on example ergonomics
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting — aligned on minimal scope and portability constraints (no heavy dependencies, <=3 files per example).
2026-02-16: Prototype Next.js streaming UI using SDK streaming client; discovered need for a small client helper to normalize chunk framing across runtimes.
2026-02-19: Implemented retry decorator pattern for Python and validated idempotency-key approach with FastAPI example; documented trade-off between at-most-once vs at-least-once semantics.

2026-02-24: Go example initial commit demonstrates streaming over HTTP/1.1 with chunked transfer; found a minor issue with SDK's default read timeout — opened ENG-864210 to track timeout config change.
2026-02-27: Added smoke CI job using a lightweight mock Redwood server (local docker) to assert streaming and retry behaviors; toggles between fast path and fallback model.
2026-03-01: Addressed DX review comments: simplified env var instructions, added example envrc, and clarified recommended retry backoff values in cookbook
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Ramirez): prefer examples to highlight cost/latency tradeoffs, add a short section showing when to pick quantized models vs lower-latency models.
Design (Lena Ortiz): Next.js UI should show partial message rendering and skeleton states; suggested accessible ARIA labels for streaming indicators.
Backend (Kofi Mensah): suggested using explicit idempotency keys for operations that mutate state and adding a small helper to attach keys automatically in SDK examples.
Security (Priya Nair): flagged that CLI examples must not hardcode keys; added note and sample .env.example and recommended KMS patterns in cookbook
